title: Chrome Can Now Pull Booking Codes and Order Numbers From Your Gmail
excerpt: Google's Gemini-powered enhanced autofill suggests flight bookings, tracking numbers and order details from your inbox as you fill forms — US-only, opt-in, and easy to switch off.
body:
• Chrome's enhanced autofill, powered by Gemini, now suggests order numbers, tracking details, flight bookings and vehicle details pulled from your Gmail while you fill in web forms.
  • It is opt-in and US-only for now: you must use Gemini in Chrome with Personal Intelligence turned on, be 18 or older, and use a personal Google account — work, school and supervised accounts are excluded.
  • Suggestions appear under a "Suggested by Gemini" label; removing a suggestion does not delete the email, but deleting the email removes the suggestion.
  • To switch it off: Chrome Settings, then Autofill and passwords, then Enhanced autofill, then turn off "Find and fill with Gemini."

Google Chrome can now fill in online forms with details it finds in your Gmail. The enhanced autofill feature, which Google began rolling out in the United States on October 28, surfaces order numbers, tracking information and flight bookings from your inbox at the moment a form asks for them, Notebookcheck reported. A traveller checking in for a flight, for example, can pick up the booking code from the confirmation email without leaving the check-in page.

The feature is powered by Gemini with Personal Intelligence, Google's opt-in setting that lets Gemini read connected Google apps such as Gmail. Chrome product manager Amanda Lim announced the rollout on Google's Chrome blog, writing that the new suggestions appear "right when you need them," alongside the names, addresses and cards autofill already offered.

Who Gets It — and Who Does Not

The gate is narrow. Enhanced autofill reaches only people in the US who use Gemini in Chrome with Personal Intelligence switched on, on desktop, Android and iOS. Users must be 18 or older and signed in with a personal Google account with Keep Activity on; work, school and supervised accounts are excluded. People in Europe will not see it for now, because Personal Intelligence is not available in the European Economic Area, Switzerland or the UK.

How the Suggestions Work

When Gemini finds a match in your inbox, the suggestion appears in the autofill dropdown under a "Suggested by Gemini" heading with the Gemini spark icon, gHacks reported. On Android, a long press on a suggestion opens two options: view sources, which opens the original email in a new tab so you can verify the details, and remove suggestion, which dismisses the entry without deleting the email. Deleting the underlying email removes the suggestion permanently. Details pulled from Gmail cannot be edited inside Chrome — if a suggestion is wrong, the fix has to happen in the source email.

Google says sensitive data is encrypted and that users remain in control. The release builds on an earlier upgrade that let autofill draw passport numbers, addresses and other details from Google accounts and Google Wallet, and Google says support for details from images in Google Photos is coming "soon," with no date given. Google first tested the capability in July in its Canary test build under the name "Find and Fill with Gemini"; the public release is narrower and uses Gmail as its only source.

The Privacy Trade-Off

The convenience is inseparable from the permission behind it: the feature works only because Gemini has been allowed to read your mail. Google's own admin documentation notes the feature also handles page content, the page URL and your interactions with suggestions. Readers who opted in to Personal Intelligence for other Gemini features may now find it active in Chrome forms as well — worth a settings check either way.

What to Watch Next

Google has not announced when enhanced autofill will reach other countries, languages or account types, or when the Google Photos support from the test build will return. For now, eligible US users will see it arrive gradually as the rollout proceeds.

steps.detail: Use the three-dot menu, then Settings.
Select Enhanced autofill inside that section.

steps.step: Turn off 'Find and fill with Gemini'
steps.detail: This stops Gmail-based suggestions while leaving regular autofill intact.
In Gemini settings, under Connected Apps, disconnect Gmail to stop Gemini reading your mail at all.
